facts.text: Powered haulage remains a leading cause of mining deaths.
facts.quote: Powered haulage is still a leading killer in mining.

facts.text: Powered haulage caused 13 of 33 US mining deaths (39%) in calendar 2025.
facts.quote: In calendar 2025 it caused 13 of 33 US mining deaths (39%)

facts.text: Powered haulage caused 426 of 4,792 nonfatal US mining injuries (9%) in calendar 2025.
facts.quote: 426 of 4,792 nonfatal injuries (9%)

facts.text: The powered-haulage accident category includes shuttle cars, locomotives, front-end loaders and similar machines and is broader than object collisions.
facts.quote: the category covers shuttle cars, locomotives, front-end loaders and similar machines and is wider than object collisions

facts.text: Powered-haulage accident statistics measure the importance of mobile-machine risk, not the share of accidents automatic braking could address.
facts.quote: so it measures the importance of mobile-machine risk rather than the share that automatic braking could address

facts.text: The deadliest mining collision pattern is a large machine running over a light vehicle or a person outside the operator's visibility.
facts.quote: The deadliest pattern is a large machine running over a light vehicle or a person it cannot see.

facts.text: US surface-mine fatality reports from 2000 to mid-2006 contain 22 blind-area deaths.
facts.quote: US surface-mine fatality reports from 2000 to mid-2006 contain 22 blind-area deaths

facts.text: Among 22 US surface-mine blind-area deaths reported from 2000 to mid-2006, dump trucks were involved in 38% and front-end loaders in 33%.
facts.quote: dump trucks were involved in 38% and front-end loaders in 33%

facts.text: Among 22 US surface-mine blind-area deaths reported from 2000 to mid-2006, 67% of victims were in the rear blind area of reversing equipment.
facts.quote: 67% of victims were in the rear blind area of reversing equipment

facts.text: US surface-mine and quarry data from 1999 to 2003 show about five blind-area deaths per year, representing 12% of all deaths at those sites.
facts.quote: Earlier data (1999 to 2003) show about five such deaths a year, 12% of all deaths at surface mines and quarries

facts.text: Dump trucks were involved in 58% of US surface-mine and quarry blind-area deaths in the 1999–2003 data.
facts.quote: Earlier data (1999 to 2003) show about five such deaths a year, 12% of all deaths at surface mines and quarries, with dump trucks involved in 58%.

facts.text: An analysis of 54 US haul-truck deaths from January 2005 to June 2021 classified 21 as involving berms, 13 as collisions with people or vehicles, 12 as occurring at dump points and eight as having other causes.
facts.quote: Of 54 US haul-truck deaths (January 2005 to June 2021), 21 involved berms, 13 were collisions with people or vehicles, 12 happened at dump points and 8 had other causes.

facts.text: Of 13 fatal US haul-truck collisions with people or vehicles in January 2005–June 2021, 12 involved a forward-moving truck.
facts.quote: Of the 13 collisions, 12 involved a forward-moving truck

facts.text: Four of the 13 fatal US haul-truck collisions with people or vehicles in January 2005–June 2021 began when the truck started moving while victims were within 50 ft (15 m).
facts.quote: four began with the truck starting to move while the victims were within 50 ft (15 m)

facts.text: In the 13 fatal US haul-truck collisions with people or vehicles in January 2005–June 2021, five victims were in light vehicles, three were pedestrians and three were in other haul trucks.
facts.quote: Five victims were in light vehicles, three were pedestrians, three were in other haul trucks.

facts.text: The claim that reversing is the main fatal mode is population-specific rather than universally applicable.
facts.quote: "Reversing is the main fatal mode" is a population statement, not a universal one.

facts.text: Cross-industry British guidance states that nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths occur during reversing.
facts.quote: Cross-industry British guidance says nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths happen during reversing

facts.text: Smaller trucks and loaders at quarries back over people, whereas very large haul trucks drive forward over light vehicles.
facts.quote: smaller trucks and loaders at quarries do back over people; very large haul trucks drive forward over light vehicles

facts.text: A collision-mitigation validation plan needs separate forward, reverse, start-from-rest, turning and swing scenarios rather than one generic proximity zone.
facts.quote: A validation plan needs separate forward, reverse, start-from-rest, turning and swing scenarios rather than one generic proximity zone.

facts.text: Most haul-truck deaths in the US surface-mining analysis for 2005–2021 were not collisions with objects.
facts.quote: Most haul-truck deaths are not collisions with objects at all.

facts.text: Berm and dump-point events accounted for 33 of 54 US haul-truck deaths in the 2005–2021 surface-mining analysis.
facts.quote: Berm and dump-point events account for 33 of the 54 haul-truck deaths

facts.text: Among 12 fatal US haul-truck dump-point cases in the 2005–2021 surface-mining analysis, six were reverse-overs and six were ground failures.
facts.quote: of the 12 dump-point cases, six were reverse-overs and six were ground failures

facts.text: Ten of the 12 fatal US haul-truck dump-point cases in the 2005–2021 surface-mining analysis involved an absent or inadequate berm.
facts.quote: ten involved an absent or inadequate berm

facts.text: Seven drivers in the 12 fatal US haul-truck dump-point cases in the 2005–2021 surface-mining analysis were unbelted.
facts.quote: seven drivers were unbelted

facts.text: A system that detects only vehicles and people addresses an important but incomplete part of haul-truck fatal risk.
facts.quote: A system that only detects vehicles and people addresses an important but incomplete part of the fatal-risk picture.

facts.text: Mining mobile-machine collisions persist despite controls, according to regulator documents and secondary reporting from Australia and South Africa.
facts.quote: Collisions persist despite controls, and regulators say so.

facts.text: In July 2023, the New South Wales regulator reported no meaningful year-on-year reduction in reported vehicle interactions.
facts.quote: The New South Wales regulator saw "no meaningful reduction" in reported vehicle interactions year on year (July 2023)

facts.text: In July 2025, the New South Wales regulator reported 30 underground coal LHD and personnel-transport collisions over 12 months.
facts.quote: recorded 30 underground coal LHD and personnel-transport collisions in 12 months (July 2025)

facts.text: Queensland reported mobile plant collisions at the top of its high-potential incident list in 2024.
facts.quote: Queensland reports mobile plant collisions at the top of its high-potential incident list (2024)

facts.text: Queensland warns that near misses involving mobile plant are under-reported.
facts.quote: warns that near misses are under-reported

facts.text: South Africa recorded nine trackless-mobile-machine deaths in 2024, up from six.
facts.quote: South Africa recorded nine trackless-mobile-machine deaths in 2024, up from six.

facts.text: Nuisance alarms are the best-documented field failure of mining warning systems.
facts.quote: Nuisance alarms are the best-documented field failure of warning systems.

facts.text: During seven days of testing on a Caterpillar 793B haul truck at a US copper mine in 2004, radar alarmed during 94% of 618 reverse movements.
facts.quote: On a Caterpillar 793B haul truck over seven days at a US copper mine (2004), radar alarmed in 94% of 618 reverse movements

facts.text: Of 580 radar alarms recorded on a Caterpillar 793B at a US copper mine during seven days in 2004, 40% warranted action, 18% were false alarms with no significant object and 42% were nuisance alarms caused by real objects posing no danger.
facts.quote: of 580 alarms, 40% warranted action, 18% were false (no significant object) and 42% were nuisance alarms (a real object but no danger)

facts.text: The audible radar alarm on a Caterpillar 793B tested at a US copper mine in 2004 was found switched off after shifts.
facts.quote: The audible alarm was found switched off after shifts.

facts.text: US underground coal workers at seven mines reported unnecessary automatic shutdowns ranging from once a day to 15 times per cut of coal.
facts.quote: Underground coal workers at seven mines reported unnecessary automatic shutdowns from once a day to 15 times per cut of coal

facts.text: At one US underground coal mine, use of an emergency-stop override had become routine.
facts.quote: at one mine an emergency-stop override had become routine

facts.text: A worker at a US underground coal mine activated an emergency-stop override 87 times before his fatal accident in June 2017.
facts.quote: had been activated 87 times by a worker before his fatal accident in June 2017
